reviewer.role: Read-only Council evidence/calibration auditor; not a new scored round

scope.method: Python stdlib arithmetic/hash/header reads, immutable Git source/diff reads, original-detail individual image views. No browser, product execution, new captures, crops, collages, package installation or pixel diff.

summary: Arithmetic and complete files-array freezes reproduce. Fifty quality and sixteen separate-fit dimension spreads affect twenty originals. Some concrete list rhythm/emphasis/wrapping remains; the score drop is not evidence of implementation regression. Stronger broken-screen, empty-space, placeholder-font and slash-only-fix claims are not supported. Preserve both reviewers and all published scores.

anchors.3: Broken: overlap/clipping/unreadable or no discernible action.
anchors.5: Works but fights: competing emphasis/mixed components/ambiguous states.
anchors.7: Solid: consistent components, minor scanning rhythm/contrast/emphasis slips.
anchors.9: Refined: every element earns emphasis, even rhythm and clear states.

authority.interpretation: Anchors guide explanations, not replacement numeric ratings. A reasonable 6/8 intermediate or independent weighting remains possible. Do not demand score convergence.

blacklists-primary.verdict: Visible no-filled-action observation supported; inference of no discernible primary or a broken task is overstated.
blacklists-primary.evidence: All four R3 originals show an underlined Add list header link and two labelled Filtering buttons; desktop also shows Enable/Refresh. Phone row actions and add form submit are below the viewport. Source layout.html links #add-list; blacklists.html:94 has that heading target and :98-112 retains the add POST and a filled submit. R2 desktop/mobile-light show the formerly filled header.
blacklists-primary.anchor_consistency: R2 requested quiet or anchor-styled list jumps with filled actual submits. R3 implements that policy. The loss of a filled header is real, especially on Blacklists with its longer introduction, but demanding one back without acknowledging the jump/submit tradeoff would undo the prior action hierarchy. A primary can be a clear link. Mild emphasis/discoverability preference is distinct from anchor 3 no discernible action or anchor 5 competing controls. Do not manufacture a new feature or promote Turn filtering off to primary.
blacklists-primary.resolution: Preserve scores. Keep actual submit primary and header jump tertiary; no Blacklists-only reversion or requirement to force the below-fold submit into the initial viewport.

blacklists-type-layout.verdict: URL split and long introduction supported; four legitimate type roles and semantic badges do not alone establish incoherent components.
blacklists-type-layout.evidence: Current desktop name/source column puts name, description and full URL together; matched R2 desktop-light has an eight-line narrow description and separate three-line URL. Current description is three lines and URL two. Current phone description is three lines and URL two. State and source type labels are readable. Desktop source-row actions are separate with clear outlines. Phone source actions are not visible.
blacklists-type-layout.anchor_consistency: Remaining wrapping/rhythm is solid-screen polish around anchor 7, with reasonable latitude at 6/8 for density. None of these originals shows overlap, clipped source text or unreadable controls. Sol coherence 9 plausibly judges a consistent vocabulary; positive components do not imply typography/density have no remaining defect. Opus color rationale itself acknowledges appropriate text-labelled neutral/warning states.
blacklists-type-layout.resolution: Preserve independent scores. Address separator-aware URL wrapping; retain description, built-in/off/never-loaded semantics and safety/trust prose. Do not delete factual copy or status distinctions to raise density.

url-wrap.verdict: Mid-token split confirmed; slash-only wrapping is not a general containment solution.
url-wrap.evidence: All four current Blacklists originals split StevenBlack at an interior letter. app.css:154 (.technical), :172 (.source-url), :366 (phone td) retain overflow-wrap:anywhere. Template :58 prints the escaped complete URL.
url-wrap.failure_mode: Inserting <wbr> after / while retaining anywhere supplies preferred soft opportunities but permits emergency interior wrapping. Removing all emergency wrapping and allowing only slash breaks leaves an arbitrarily long hostname, slash-free path segment, query value or fragment wider than the column; min-width:0 does not split that token. Merely adding wbr also does not remove inherited anywhere rules.
url-wrap.resolution: Prefer natural separator breaks while retaining an emergency overflow-wrap fallback and the complete readable/copyable URL. Keep min-width:0 containment. Do not promise exclusively slash breaks or arbitrary URL containment without rendering verification. No dependency, truncation or unsafe raw HTML is warranted.

row-type.verdict: Small mono/sans size and baseline mismatch supported; blanket mixed-face defect and different Record placeholder faces are not supported.
row-type.evidence: Services/Records desktop have smaller technical names/addresses beside larger sans all views; phone baselines likewise differ. app.css:153 table body uses --ky-type-body (0.9375rem); :154 technical uses --ky-type-meta (0.8125rem). These are nominal 15/13px at a 16px root, not Opus exact 15/14px assertions. Mono is explicitly appropriate for DNS values. Records template :30 and :36 are both input[type=text]; app.css:215-218 assigns both the same IBM Plex Mono stack, with no rname/rvalue or placeholder font override in the shipped stylesheets inspected. :36 changes placeholder color only.
row-type.anchor_consistency: Treat actual 2px data/meta rhythm differences as minor scanning polish, not proof of four conflicting design systems or anchor 5 fighting components. Pixel-estimated font identities/sizes are not CSS measurements. Sol typography 8 recognizes appropriate semantic distinction; Opus 6 is stricter judgment, not newly established breakage.
row-type.resolution: Align shared row metadata size/line-height and baseline while preserving semantic mono for DNS data and sans prose. Reject the proposed placeholder-face repair. Records precedence note starts at the section edge by design; paragraph :44-45 is outside the form, not a malformed field. Moving it is optional and excluded from the smallest batch.

phone-rhythm.verdict: Staggered metadata baselines and extra action-row space are supported in all four Services/Records phone originals.
phone-rhythm.evidence: Services has Address/View and Aliases/Routing offsets; 40px routing summary and its inline label produce a larger second-row offset. Records Type badge sits below the adjacent Value baseline; Remove occupies a separate row after View. app.css:364-374 uses two grid columns with block/inline cells, a flex details cell and a trailing actions grid cell. Matched R2 Services-mobile-light and Records-mobile-dark show the same metadata structure; new chevron/text Remove and a slightly taller phone header do not create it.
phone-rhythm.anchor_consistency: Rows stay readable and within the image, with correctly paired labels and fields. This is rhythm/density polish, compatible with anchor 7 and intermediate judgments, not broken containment or demonstrated inaccessible actions. A separate action line can be reasonable when needed for a target/disclosure.
phone-rhythm.resolution: Use common row tracks and baseline alignment; bring action placement into the row rhythm when it fits. Preserve minimum target geometry, every field, native details expansion and table/header semantics. Do not shrink targets or force open routing forms into a single line. Blacklists current Format/Entries and Last update/State pairing is already readable; do not restructure it without a specific remaining mismatch.

danger-color.verdict: Dark warm red/orange proximity is real; semantic ambiguity or required token redesign is not established.
danger-color.evidence: Both dark Services/Records pairs show warm salmon Remove and orange Add link. On desktop the commit is filled and Remove outlined; on phones only the underlined header jump and red text Remove appear, while filled submit is below-fold. Labels, fill/outline and placement remain distinct. base.html:11-16 loads tokens.css after app.css; tokens.css:91-107 aliases --danger to --ky-danger for Busnes/OS states. Dark shared danger #ff8176 differs from accent #f5865f.
danger-color.anchor_consistency: A minor contrast/emphasis concern can justify a stricter color judgment. Similar hue alone is not proof a scanning user cannot tell Remove from Add, nor a contrast-gate failure. Opus phone language describing the filled submit beside Remove exceeds the viewport evidence. Sol color 8 already acknowledges competing salience.
danger-color.resolution: Preserve both judgments. Neutralizing secondary header links is the smallest local relief. Do not change vendored/shared danger tokens or weaken destructive semantics in this product batch; any future shared palette work needs its own evidence.

list-accent.verdict: Secondary header links still use accent; actual-submit promotion is implemented.
list-accent.evidence: Services/Records all four originals show orange underlined jumps; desktop also shows filled actual submit. app.css:88 establishes link geometry/underline without overriding global a color at :328. layout.html:40-42 removes button class; Records :42 and Services :60 remove ghost from actual submits.
list-accent.anchor_consistency: The literal orange-only-primary/selection/focus contract supports neutral secondary jumps more directly than Sol generic next-step exception on pages with an actual primary. On phone, jump is the only initial-viewport add entry, so its clarity must remain when neutralized. Selected navigation/stamp are separate legitimate marks, not duplicate committing actions.
list-accent.resolution: Use neutral ink for these three tertiary jumps, retain underline/target and focus, preserve the filled actual submits. No labels, routes or behavior changes.

dashboard-coherence.verdict: One flat component vocabulary supported; repetition and sparse data do not establish incoherence.
dashboard-coherence.evidence: All four current Dashboard originals have aligned metric groups, neutral numbers and consistently framed charts. R2 desktop/mobile-light comparison and source diff show shared five-column metric tracks and removal of phone inset.
